Year 7 Science · Unit plan

Unit: Biodiversity & Ecosystems

7 weeks · 11 lessons, a unit review and the CAT · Victorian Curriculum F–10 v2.0

Students learn how living things are told apart, named and classified, then follow matter and energy through Victorian ecosystems — food webs, ecosystem services and adaptations — before tracing how introduced species and human activity threaten biodiversity and evaluating how we conserve it. A Research Portfolio on the Eastern Barred Bandicoot is built stage by stage across the unit and is the preparation for the CAT, an Ecosystem Investigation on a species students have not studied.

Achievement standard · Levels 7–8

  • Science Understanding. Explain how biological diversity is ordered and organised, using classification tools including dichotomous keys; represent flows of matter and energy in ecosystems with food webs, and explain how changes in biotic and abiotic factors, including introduced species, habitat loss and climate change, affect populations.
  • Science Inquiry. Represent information with keys and models; analyse patterns; evaluate claims; construct evidence-based arguments from secondary data; communicate ideas for a purpose and audience.
  • Science as a Human Endeavour. Examine how people with different perspectives and worldviews, including First Nations knowledge, contribute to science; discuss the ethical, environmental, social and economic considerations of responses to a socio-scientific issue; analyse how science communication shapes viewpoints, policies and regulations.

Content descriptors

VC2S8U01
Similarities and differences within and between groups of organisms; classification tools, including dichotomous keys, order and organise the diversity of life
VC2S8U04
Matter and energy flow through ecosystems (food webs, food pyramids); populations are affected by changing biotic and abiotic factors, including habitat loss, climate change and introduced or removed species
VC2S8H02
Multidisciplinary endeavours draw on different perspectives and worldviews — the Caring for Country slide in every lesson
VC2S8H03
Proposed scientific responses to socio-scientific issues involve ethical, environmental, social and economic considerations
VC2S8H04
Science communication shapes individual viewpoints, community policies and regulations
VC2S8I04–I08
Science inquiry — representations including keys and models (I04); analysing patterns (I05); evaluating claims (I06); evidence-based arguments using secondary data (I07); communicating for a purpose (I08)
VC2S6U02
Levels 5–6, consolidation — structural features and behaviours that let organisms survive (Lesson 8 adaptations)

Prepare for learning

  • Optional diagnostic: pre-unit check on classification.
  • Every deck from Lesson 2 opens with a 5-minute spaced retrieval warm-up.

Review and reflect

  • Worksheet per lesson, checked in class; Stile check-ins; exit passes.
  • 60-mark unit review under test conditions; the Retrieval Quiz (200 questions, filter by topic) for revision.

Modifications for DI and IEPs

  • Booklet scaffold boxes; Stile Glossary: Classification and biodiversity; glossary flashcards; Handwriting Practice — Biodiversity & Ecosystems.
  • Impact chains and food webs built one link at a time on screen; pre-drawn frames to fill in; sentence stems.
  • Before the CAT: the stage → CAT part map printed in the front of the Research Portfolio.

Extension

  • Worksheet questions marked Year 8 extension; the Above The Level prompt in each portfolio stage.
  • The Year 8 extension parts of the CAT, banded separately by the rubric tool.

Print the whole thing

  • Whole Student Booklet (52 pp.)
  • Worksheet Booklet — all 11 worksheets
  • Research Portfolio
  • Species Profile — Eastern Barred Bandicoot

Each lesson row links its own booklet pages for printing one section at a time.

  • Every lesson carries a Caring for Country / First Nations perspectives slide with a matching booklet page — core, not optional (VC2S8H02).
  • No practicals in this unit yet. The audit requires experiments to be documented with an inquiry LI, a RiskAssess and an activity sheet; none are planned here. Add a practical (e.g. quadrat or leaf-litter sampling) or the 2027 Botanic Gardens / CERES excursion, with RiskAssess
